catalog_entry.label: NHL draft selections (top pick and draft slot)
catalog_entry.target: Which player or team is selected at a given draft position, determined by the league's lottery and team decisions.
catalog_entry.mechanism: Draft slots come from the standings-weighted lottery and pick ownership; each holding club then chooses from a prospect board whose consensus is tight at the top and loose in the middle of round one, with club needs, general-manager habits, medical flags and late trades deciding between close names. Nothing about on-ice performance enters beyond final standings.

inputs.why: The lottery odds by final standing and ownership fix who owns each slot and the probability of moving up before selection.
Which club actually holds each first-round slot after trades, protections and forfeitures decides which team can select.
Independent scouting-service rankings are the prior over which prospect goes at each slot and how reliably consensus is followed.
The tightness of the board around a slot converts a rank gap into a calibrated selection probability.
Positional and pipeline need breaks ties between near-equal prospects at flat parts of the board.
A club's history of reaching for or following consensus changes how its pick is distributed.
Late changes of pick holder change which club selects and sometimes who moves up the order.
Eligibility, medical and signing-path flags explain slides from the consensus rank.
The pre-lottery distribution of final standings determines the pool of lottery teams and their odds before the lottery is run.
Draft-week reports of a club's intentions are the main late signal on the top picks, and their reliability varies by source.
Class-specific base rate that the consensus first-ranked prospect goes first overall, by era, guards against overconfidence.
Lottery date, combine and draft day set when each information source arrives and when the contract can resolve.
Roster, coaching and front-office news changes club needs and may signal trades of picks before draft day.
Age-curve evidence on prospects' development paths informs how clubs weigh upside against readiness.
Reference class for league-office process markets: how often the officially scheduled event happens as planned.

interactions.hypothesis: A rank gap only means a confident pick when dispersion is small; when the top two prospects are separated by little compared with service disagreement, the same gap yields a near coin-flip, while a large gap with tight dispersion gives near certainty.

The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.

Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.

A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add.

contract.settlement_definition: No rules text was sampled for KXNHLDRAFTTOP (Pro Hockey Top Pick) or KXNHLDRAFTPICK (Pro Hockey Draft Pick). From the titles, the contracts presumably settle on who or which club is announced at first overall or at a named slot by the league; the player-versus-club basis, treatment of traded picks, and the source of truth are unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: Top Pick versus Draft Pick: the first is probably slot 1, the second a configurable slot or ladder; the strike structure is not visible.
If a pick is traded before announcement or the selection is traded afterwards, the contract may settle on the original club, the selecting club, or the receiving club; wording unknown.
A forfeited or voided pick, or a draft postponed beyond the market close, could void or delay settlement; no rules text to confirm.
contract.settlement_data_source: Presumably the league's official draft announcement, NHL.com; unverified for these series.

mechanism.summary: A draft selection is the end of a chain: final standings and a weighted lottery produce slot order, trades and protections assign each slot to a club, independent scouting services and club staff form a board, and each holding club chooses from the remaining prospects using the board, positional need, staff habit and late information such as medical news. The chain is mostly institutional rather than athletic, so the outcome is a categorical choice whose probability is sharp at the top of the board and diffuse in the middle of the first round. Information arrives in jumps: lottery night, the combine and draft-week reports.

stages.name: Pre-lottery standings fix the lottery pool and odds
stages.description: Final regular-season standings (points percentage, then tiebreakers) determine which non-playoff clubs enter the lottery and each club's odds of winning a draw. Clubs that make the playoffs, or whose picks are owned by others through trades, do not hold their own slot. This stage is a deterministic function of the last games of the season plus rules; the only variability comes from late-season results and from the tie-breaking order.
stages.distribution: Discrete ordering over 32 clubs; near-deterministic after the final game, with ties resolved by rule.

stages.name: Lottery draws and ownership assignment
stages.description: The league's weighted lottery draws for the top slots; non-winning lottery clubs fall in order of standing, with a maximum number of positions a club can rise. After the draws, pick ownership (trades, protected picks, forfeitures) assigns each slot to a holding club. The draw is genuinely random with published odds; ownership is a legal fact that may be conditional until resolved.
stages.distribution: Weighted random draw without replacement; only top slots random, remaining slots a deterministic order with ownership overlay.

stages.name: Prospect board formation and consensus
stages.description: Scouting services and the clubs' own staff rank the eligible prospects; independent public rankings converge near the draft but are uncertain months before. Eligibility, injuries and signing paths remove or demote some players. The board is a noisy ordering with very different spread at the top than in the middle of round one.
stages.distribution: Ranked order with slot-dependent dispersion; tight at the top, wide in the middle and late first round.

stages.name: Club decision rule: board, need and staff style
stages.description: Each holding club chooses from the remaining board using its own ranking (partly consensus, partly staff-specific preferences), roster and pipeline need, and an appetite for risk. Between close prospects need and staff habit decide; at the top the choice is nearly forced by consensus. Clubs also decide whether to trade the pick or trade up, which changes the selecting club.
stages.distribution: Categorical choice over the remaining board; concentrated at slot 1-3, spread across 3-8 names in the middle of round one.

stages.name: Late information and settlement on announcement
stages.description: In the final days, insider reports, combine news and trade rumours move the likelihood of particular selections; the outcome settles when the league announces the pick at the draft. Settlement may depend on the exact wording: player named, club making the selection, slot number, and whether a pick traded after being made counts for the original club.
stages.distribution: Binary resolution after a discrete announcement; late reports shift probabilities in jumps, not smoothly.

talent_strength.note: Prospect quality enters as the consensus order and its spread, not as on-ice performance of the selecting club.

opponent_matchup.note: There is no opponent in a draft selection; the only interaction is between the holding club's needs and the remaining board, handled under role_personnel.

role_personnel.note: Club needs and decision-maker habits determine the selection among close prospects.

availability_news.note: Medical, eligibility and draft-week reporting change who is available at a slot.

coaching_scheme.note: On-ice coaching tactics do not decide draft choices; the relevant staff effect is the general manager and scouting director behaviour captured in gm_draft_behavior_history.

environment.note: Venue, weather and travel have no bearing on a draft selection made at a league event; no environmental variable alters the outcome.

game_context_script.note: No game is played; there is no score state, pace or overtime. The comparable timeline structure is the lottery-then-draft sequence in the calendar.

pace_volume.note: No count of events accumulates; the outcome is one selection per slot, not a volume of shots, possessions or plays over a window.

efficiency_conversion.note: No conversion rate generates the outcome; the closest idea, how often consensus translates into the actual pick, is a distribution calibrator under distribution_variance.

distribution_variance.note: Slot-level dispersion of rank versus actual pick is the distribution of the outcome.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Standings stakes determine the pool, and the timeline of lottery and draft day sets when trades and information arrive.

officiating_rules.note: League lottery rules (draws, max positions risen, win limits) and pick-ownership rules play the role of rules governing the process.

settlement_contract.note: Whether the contract is settled on the player, club or slot, and how trades are treated, depends on rules text that was not sampled; see unresolved.

nhl.draft_team_need_profile.label: Club organisational need profile at the pick (positions, prospect pipeline depth, window)
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.mechanism: Translates a club's current roster, prospect pool and competitive window into position and archetype preferences when two or more prospects are close on the board.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.rationale: Early picks are mostly decided by consensus, but between near-tied prospects clubs lean toward centre/defence scarcity or toward a pipeline gap. The subtlety is that NHL clubs historically claim to take best available, so the need effect is small at the top and grows only where the board is flat.
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.measurement: For each club holding a first-round pick compute, as of draft week, (a) count and quality (draft-pedigree-weighted) of signed or drafted prospects aged <=22 by position C/W/D/G, (b) NHL roster age and contract-expiry profile by position over the next 3 seasons, (c) rebuild-vs-contend flag from last-two-season points%. Express as a position-need z-score vs league mean; shrink to zero with k=3 historical picks per club-position cell to avoid noise; freeze at the draft-order-final timestamp.
free_sources: Elite Prospects team prospect pools (free tier)
raw_data: club prospect pool table: player, position, age, draft slot
NHL roster and contract table
team standings points% by season
nhl.draft_team_need_profile.why: Differentiates which of two close prospects a particular club takes at a specific slot, and so which club ends up with the contested player.

nhl.draft_board_dispersion.label: Dispersion of public draft rankings around each prospect's slot
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.mechanism: Measures how tight or fractured the independent scouting-service rankings are around the slots in question; the tighter the consensus, the more the pick behaves as a deterministic read of the board.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.rationale: Mean rank hides whether the top is a one-prospect consensus or a three-way debate. Slot-level variance is what turns a rank gap into a probability of selection, and it is much smaller at first overall than at slot 12 where historical misses by slot are large.
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.measurement: For each prospect pool at the as-of date collect the ranks from at least 4 independent services (e.g. NHL Central Scouting, Elite Prospects, McKeen's, Bob McKenzie/TSN consensus, FC Hockey) and compute cross-service mean rank, standard deviation, and gap between the k-th and (k+1)-th mean ranks. Back-test calibration with the historical frequency that the consensus rank-k prospect went exactly at slot k, bucketed by slot 1, 2-3, 4-10, 11-32, pooled 2005-present, with Laplace shrinkage of 1 pseudo-count per bucket.
free_sources: Wikipedia draft history for actual slots
raw_data: service ranks by prospect and publication date
actual draft slot by prospect and year
nhl.draft_board_dispersion.why: Sets the width of the selection probability around the consensus rank for a specific draft slot, the core of both the top-pick and slot contracts.

nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.label: Probability a held pick changes club or slot before selection
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.mechanism: Estimates the chance the slot is traded to another club (or the selection traded post-pick) between the lottery and the selection call, changing which club makes the pick.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.rationale: Contracts that settle on which team selects, rather than which player, depend on pick ownership at the moment the pick is announced. Picks are frequently moved on draft day, and top-3 picks move rarely but non-zero, so a static ownership table is not a final answer.
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.measurement: From the draft-pick transaction history 2005-present compute, per slot bucket (1-3, 4-10, 11-20, 21-32), the share of picks that changed club within the 14 days before selection and on draft day, separated by whether the holding club is a seller or buyer by points% rank. Add a club-level multiplier from past count of draft-day trades per GM, shrunk to league with k=4 drafts. As-of the ownership table timestamp; zero out if the contract rules define the selecting club by pre-lottery ownership.
raw_data: pick transaction log with date, from-club, to-club, slot
GM tenure table
nhl.draft_pick_trade_hazard.why: Needed because a slot contract on a team can resolve against the club that holds the pick at announcement, which differs from the lottery winner after a trade.

nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.label: Prospect eligibility, signing-rights and medical availability flags
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.mechanism: Captures whether each prospect is eligible for the given draft, has no contractual or injury obstacle to being taken at a high slot.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.rationale: A top prospect with a major injury, an age-eligibility edge case, or a contract-rights complication can slide by several slots. The slide is asymmetric: clubs seldom move a prospect up for reasons of health.
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.measurement: For each of the top-40 prospects as-of the draft combine and the week before the draft, record binary or ordinal flags: eligible (born by the cut-off date), over-ager status, injury within last 12 months with games missed share, combine medical concerns reported, and signing-path complexity (CHL vs NCAA vs European contract). Convert to an expected slot slide in positions via a regression on historical prospects with the same flag class, shrunk with k=10 prospects per class.
raw_data: prospect birthdate and draft year
injury and games-missed log
combine report flags
nhl.prospect_eligibility_medical_flags.why: Moves probability mass off a prospect whose slot is being priced, and onto the next name on the board.

nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.label: General-manager and scouting-staff draft behaviour history
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.mechanism: Learns how often a club's decision-makers deviate from the consensus board and in which direction (upside, size, age, nationality) from their past selections.
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.rationale: A club that has repeatedly reached for specific archetypes makes a different pick than the board implies; consensus-following clubs follow the board. The GM and head scout identity matters because staff turnover resets the habit.
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.measurement: Over the last 8 drafts, per club-staff regime compute (a) mean signed difference between actual slot and consensus rank, (b) share of first-round picks that were outside the consensus top-N for that slot, (c) preference weights for size/age/league by regression on the consensus residual. Shrink to league with k=6 picks, reset on a change of GM or director of amateur scouting, and apply only to the slot where the club selects.
raw_data: draft picks by club: slot, consensus rank
front-office staff tenure
nhl.gm_draft_behavior_history.why: Turns the board into a club-specific selection distribution when the contract settles on a named club's pick.

nhl.draft_lottery_odds_by_standing.reason: Directly generates the slot-ownership order: odds are fixed by pre-lottery standing and the lottery draw is the only random step upstream of club choices.

nhl.pick_ownership_and_protection.reason: Needed to map a slot to the club that selects; pick protections and conditional swaps change the holder and are written down before the draft.

nhl.prospect_consensus_ranking.reason: The best public prior over who is selected at each slot; the catalog label already includes selection agreement history, which is the right target.

nhl.season_sim_distribution.reason: Useful only before the season ends, to price lottery-pool membership; once the lottery is run it adds nothing, so it is a time-limited input.

nhl.insider_report_credibility.reason: Draft-week insider claims about the first pick are the main late information; credibility and lag weighting is what stops reports from being over- or under-weighted.

nhl.reference_class_hazard.reason: Provides the historical agreement rate between consensus and the actual pick by era; a context calibrator, not a driver of any individual pick.

nhl.announcement_calendar.reason: Gives the timeline (lottery, combine, draft day) that determines when information resolves; does not move the probability itself.

nhl.news.reason: Generic transactions feed; relevant mainly for front-office changes and pick trades, otherwise noisy for draft slots.

nhl.career_trajectory.reason: Built for NHL age curves and rookie ramps; for amateur prospects the decision uses scouting reports and junior production, so this only weakly informs club choice.

nhl.offfield_base_rate.reason: Generic off-ice base rate; draft happening on schedule is near-certain, so it adds little beyond the calendar for slot-selection contracts.

interactions.mechanism: A rank gap only means a confident pick when dispersion is small; when the top two prospects are separated by little compared with service disagreement, the same gap yields a near coin-flip, while a large gap with tight dispersion gives near certainty.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit selection probability on the rank gap alone vs gap divided by cross-service standard deviation and compare log-loss over drafts 2005-present, split by slot 1 and slots 2-10.

interactions.mechanism: The probability a club selects at a slot is the lottery probability of that slot times the chance the club still owns the pick after protections resolve; protections only bind for specific lottery outcomes, so ownership and draw outcomes are jointly distributed, not independent.
interactions.how_to_test: Enumerate lottery draw outcomes for a historical year with a protected pick and compare the marginal-by-product probability vs the joint enumeration of draw-and-protection outcomes.

interactions.mechanism: Club need only decides the pick when the board is flat around the slot; below a dispersion threshold the consensus pick is taken regardless of need, so the need effect switches on at mid-first-round slots and is absent at the top.
interactions.how_to_test: Add need x flatness interaction and test whether the need coefficient is zero for slots 1-3 and positive for slots 8-20 in a conditional logit over remaining prospects.

interactions.mechanism: A reach-prone general manager makes insider reports of an off-board choice more credible, and a consensus-following manager makes them less credible; credibility of the report and the club's historical reaching multiply rather than add.
interactions.how_to_test: Back-test reported-pick accuracy by source for reach-prone vs consensus-following clubs and test an interaction term in the pick model.

interactions.mechanism: Before the lottery, trade hazard concerns picks of unknown slot and is low for top slots; after the lottery and especially on draft day it concentrates on known slots, so the hazard regime changes at the lottery date and again on draft day.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate pick-change frequency separately in windows before lottery, between lottery and draft day, and on draft day, and test slot x window interaction.

nonlinearities.shape: Dispersion rises steeply from slot 1 to slot 5, then flattens across mid-round slots, so selection probability for the consensus rank-k name falls convexly with k
nonlinearities.why: Historical agreement between consensus rank and actual slot is much higher at the very top than in the middle of round one, so a linear rank effect would overstate mid-round confidence.

nonlinearities.shape: Odds of winning the first draw are heavily concentrated in the worst few clubs and then decay slowly, with a cap on positions a club can rise
nonlinearities.why: The published odds are not proportional to standing; the cap on movement and two draws make the mapping from points rank to slot piecewise and non-linear.

nonlinearities.shape: Need effect saturates: beyond a modest positional deficit extra need adds little because clubs rarely reach more than a few slots
nonlinearities.why: Clubs trade need off against board value; a large need does not translate into proportionally larger reach, so the effect is bounded.

catalog_entry.label: NHL playoff series aggregate outcomes (series total goals and related series-length props)
catalog_entry.target: A quantity added up across one best-of-7 playoff series (e.g. total goals in all games) compared with a threshold. Its value depends jointly on the number of games played (4-7) and on scoring in each game.
catalog_entry.mechanism: The total is a sum over a random number of games: the rating gap and goaltending set per-game win probabilities and therefore the 4-7 game length distribution, while the same quantities set the per-game goal mean, which is lowered by the playoff environment and shifted by series state, adjustments and overtime. Closer series run longer and produce more goals, so length and goals are jointly distributed.

inputs.why: Live series state (score, games played, home ice, rest, lineup) determines how many games remain and the goals already banked.
The probability of 4, 5, 6 or 7 games sets how many games contribute to the total.
Team strength gap determines per-game win probability and so series length and, through goal means, per-game scoring.
The goaltender is the largest controllable driver of both goals against and series length in the playoffs.
Per-game goal totals are overdispersed with home-away correlation; the series sum inherits that dispersion.
Playoff scoring runs lower than the regular season with fewer penalties and continuous overtime; this fixes the per-game goal mean.
Trailing, elimination and game-seven states shift the per-game goal rate in ways the series score reveals.
Overtime periods add goals and games in the sum, with a frequency that depends on tie risk.
Adjustments across the series change scoring by game index, which matters for later games in a long series.
Shot-quality creation sets team goal means with less noise than raw goals.
Shot-quality suppression sets the opponent's goal mean and the series total.
Goaltending variance beyond binomial widens the series length distribution and the goal total.
Attempts per 60 for the pair controls shots and so goals, and drops in playoff matchups.
Power-play and penalty-kill matchups produce a share of playoff goals despite fewer penalties.
Penalty frequency determines power-play opportunities, a large source of variance in goals.
Injuries to stars and goalies mid-series change per-game strength and thus length and goals.
Empty-net goals add to totals and are more frequent in elimination games.
The year-level scoring level recalibrates the goal mean of every game.

interactions.hypothesis: A larger rating gap shortens the series (fewer games to add) while it also raises the favourite's scoring and lowers the underdog's, so total goals depend on length and per-game mean jointly: the product E[N]*mu is not the sum of separate effects, since length and goals are correlated through the gap.

An elite goalie lowers goals against, but when goalie volatility is high a hot or cold streak shifts both the number of games and the goals per game in the same direction, so mean quality and volatility multiply in effect on the total's spread.

Empty-net goals are rare in neutral states but common when a team trails by one late in an elimination game; the empty-net contribution to goals is concentrated in the elimination states, so its effect depends on series state.

Overtime probability peaks when teams are closely matched and the regulation tie probability is highest; below a rating-gap threshold OT frequency is flat, above it falls, so the rating gap acts on OT goals nonlinearly.

contract.settlement_definition: No rules text was sampled for KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOAL (NHL Series Total Goals). From the title, the contract probably settles on the number of goals scored across all games of a playoff series versus a threshold; the strike construction, whether overtime goals count, what happens to an unfinished series and the source of truth are unverified.
variants_and_edge_cases: Overtime goals: playoff overtime is sudden-death with no shootout; the contract may count all goals or regulation only, which changes totals in about a fifth of games.
Series length is random (4-7 games): the threshold may be a single total across variable length, so a sweep is mechanically lower than a seven-game series.
Siblings (Series Total Games, Game Spread, Exact Score, Series Overtime, KXNHLSERIESTOTALGOALS) are not in the sampled pack and may use different strikes or per-team goals.
contract.settlement_data_source: Presumably official NHL game results at NHL.com; unverified for this series.

mechanism.summary: The series total is a compound sum: the number of games played (4 to 7) times, in effect, per-game goals, where both depend on the same pair of teams. Team and goalie quality produce per-game win probabilities, which, with the 2-2-1-1-1 home pattern and correlated goaltending, give the length distribution; the same quality and playoff environment give a goal mean per game that shifts with series state, coaching adjustment and overtime. Because the sum has a random number of terms that correlates with the per-game mean, its distribution is wider and skewed relative to a fixed-length total.

stages.name: Per-game strength and goal means for the pair
stages.description: Each game's expected goals for and against come from the two teams' attack and suppression quality, the starting goalies, special teams and the playoff scoring environment, which runs below the regular season. This stage produces the mean total per game and the home-away split; it is where team ratings, shot quality and goaltending enter, and it does not yet know how many games will be played.
stages.distribution: Poisson-like goal counts per team with overdispersion and a positive home-away correlation.

stages.name: Win probability, home-ice sequence and series length
stages.description: Per-game win probabilities, combined with the 2-2-1-1-1 home-ice pattern and dependence between games, determine whether the series ends in 4, 5, 6 or 7 games. Closer matchups mean longer series, so the same pair rating gap that sets per-game goals also sets the number of games. Series are positively correlated through goaltending runs, so seven-game tails are thicker than binomial.
stages.distribution: Discrete distribution on {4,5,6,7} games, skewed toward 5-6 for lopsided pairs and toward 6-7 for even pairs.

stages.name: State-dependent scoring through the series
stages.description: Goals per game shift with the series score and game index: elimination games raise empty-net risk and goalie pulls, early games reflect regular-season matchups, later games reflect coaching adjustments and fatigue. The state also feeds back into length: a team trailing 0-3 produces a short series. This stage maps series trajectories to goals per game and makes the sum depend on the path.
stages.distribution: Path-dependent mixture; per-game mean shifts by a few percent by state, and the sum has covariance across games.

stages.name: Overtime periods and settlement counting
stages.description: Tied games go to sudden-death five-on-five overtime periods with no shootout, so each OT game adds at least one goal and possibly several periods of events. Whether the contract counts overtime goals, and when a series that is stopped, postponed or not completed settles, decides the mapped total. The OT frequency depends on tie probability, which rises with evenly matched teams.
stages.distribution: Geometric number of overtime periods per tied game; OT adds one deciding goal plus any pre-OT regulation goals.

talent_strength.note: Team and goalie quality set the goal means and the per-game win probability.

opponent_matchup.note: Pair-specific special-teams and adjustment effects are the matchup channel across a repeated series.

role_personnel.note: Availability of key skaters and the starting goalie changes the pair's goal mean; individual player roles are second-order for a series sum.

availability_news.note: Mid-series injuries and goalie changes change per-game strength; the series state tracks the lineup.

coaching_scheme.note: Between-game adjustments and elimination-game tactics alter scoring by game index and state.

environment.note: Playoff environment and season scoring level set the goal mean; arena effects are small and left as context.

game_context_script.note: Series trajectory, game index and empty-net behaviour are the script of the aggregate.

pace_volume.note: Volume has two scales: attempts per game and number of games, and the second is specific to this contract.

efficiency_conversion.note: Finishing and goaltending conversion determine goals from shot volume, with regression to a team mean.

distribution_variance.note: The sum of a random number of overdispersed games gives a compound distribution with heavier tails.

situational_schedule_motivation.note: Elimination, rest between games and travel in the round structure affect goals game by game.

officiating_rules.note: Playoff crews call fewer penalties, and sudden-death overtime format is the rule that creates multi-period games.

settlement_contract.note: OT counting and series-completion rules unknown without rules text; the input allows both regulation-only and total-goal conventions.

nhl.series_game_count_pmf.label: Series length distribution (P of 4, 5, 6, 7 games) from per-game win probabilities and home-ice pattern
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.mechanism: Builds the probability that a best-of-seven ends in exactly 4, 5, 6 or 7 games from each game's win probability, with the 2-2-1-1-1 home sequence and between-game dependence.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.rationale: Total goals is a sum over a random number of games, so the length distribution is the first-order driver of the mean. The subtlety is that games within a series are not independent Bernoulli draws: goaltending streaks, injuries and adjustments create correlation that fattens the 7-game tail relative to a binomial.
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.measurement: For each series compute per-game home win probabilities p_h(g) from team ratings, goalie, injuries and venue (as-of the pre-series timestamp), then enumerate paths through 2-2-1-1-1 to get P(len=n). Add dependence by mixing: with weight w=0.25 apply a common series-level shock to the log-odds with sd 0.15 (fit on 2005-present series, check the 7-game share ~ 20% of series). Report the length pmf and its expected value; recompute after each game conditional on the score.
raw_data: series results by year with game count
team ratings by date
home-ice sequence by round
nhl.series_game_count_pmf.why: Supplies the distribution of the number of summed games, which multiplies the per-game goal mean.

nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.label: Series-state effect on per-game goal rate (elimination, trailing team, game-7 intensity)
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.mechanism: Adjusts expected goals per game for the series score, since trailing and elimination games change risk-taking, line usage, goaltending changes and empty-net frequency.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.rationale: A series that is 3-0 behaves differently from 1-1: the trailing team pulls goalies earlier and the leader sits back, but the state is also what lengthens or shortens the series. The effect on goals is mixed across directions, so it must be measured rather than assumed.
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.measurement: From playoff games 2008-present tag each game by series score entering the game (e.g. 0-0, 1-0, 1-1, 2-1, 3-0, 3-1, 3-2, 3-3) and elimination flag; regress total goals per game (regulation plus OT) on state dummies, team rating-implied goal mean and venue, with a team random effect. Shrink small cells with k=15 games to the pooled mean; report multiplicative shift factors by state with standard errors.
free_sources: NHL API play-by-play and game results
raw_data: playoff game results with series score entering game
play-by-play with empty-net goals and goalie pull times
nhl.series_state_scoring_shift.why: Provides the conditional adjustment of the summed goals per game, which cannot be read from the single-game total archetype.

nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution.label: Playoff overtime frequency and length (number of 20-minute periods) and goals added
nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution.mechanism: Models how many extra periods each tied game plays and the goals scored in them, since playoff overtime is sudden-death, 5v5 and can run multiple periods.
nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution.rationale: Series totals can include overtime goals and extra periods; one overtime goal is a game decided by exactly one goal added to regulation total, and a multi-overtime game adds more events. Whether these goals count for settlement is unverified, but exposure is material in close series.
nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution.measurement: From playoff games 2005-present, compute per game P(OT) as a function of rating gap and series state, the distribution of OT periods played (1, 2, 3+) with geometric tail fit on the per-period hazard, and mean goals in overtime (exactly one by sudden death, plus any regulation-tied goals count preserved). Shrink team-level OT propensity with k=30 games; separate regulation goals from OT goals so both settlement conventions can be priced.
free_sources: NHL API game summaries and play-by-play
raw_data: playoff game periods played, OT goals, game ids
regulation tie status by game
nhl.playoff_ot_length_distribution.why: Separates regulation goals from overtime goals, which matter if the strike counts only regulation or all goals.

nhl.series_adjustment_regime.label: Coaching adjustment and matchup learning across games in a series
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.mechanism: Captures how coaches change lines, matchups, special-teams assignments and goalie decisions between games, shifting pace and goals as the series progresses.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.rationale: Early series games are sampled with the regular-season matchup profile; later games reflect adjustments and fatigue, and the typical drift in scoring across game number is not zero. Home last-change opportunity compounds this.
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.measurement: Compute from playoff games 2010-present the average change in goals per game from game 1-2 to game 5-7 conditioning on round, and the team coach-level adjustment effect measured as residual of scoring versus rating prediction at game index k. Use a team-coach random effect with shrinkage k=20 games, windows over four seasons, and exclude games played after a goalie change from the baseline.
raw_data: playoff game results by game index
line combinations and goalie by game
coach tenure
nhl.series_adjustment_regime.why: Allows scoring to drift with game index rather than assuming constant per-game goals across the series.

nhl.series_context.reason: State of the series (games played, goals banked so far, home sequence) is exactly the conditioning information for a live total; before the series it supplies the home-ice sequence.

nhl.ratings.reason: Drives per-game win probability, which sets the length distribution; the rating gap is the main reason a series total depends on the pair.

nhl.goalie_quality.reason: Playoff goals are largely a function of goalies; goals saved above expected feeds both goal mean and the chance of lopsided games.

nhl.total_goal_dispersion.reason: Gives the per-game goal variance and correlation between teams; without it the series sum variance would be understated.

nhl.playoff_context.reason: Playoff environment (tighter benches, fewer penalties, sudden-death OT) shifts the goal mean below regular-season levels; it also indicates OT format.

nhl.xg_for.reason: Process-based scoring measure; partially overlaps with ratings, so it adds mainly by separating shot quality from finishing.

nhl.xg_against.reason: Same as xg_for for the defensive side; useful but correlated with goalie quality in how it is measured.

nhl.series_goalie_volatility.reason: Directly relevant: goalie performance clusters within series, widening both length and total relative to independent games.

nhl.pace.reason: Attempt volume sets scoring chances; playoff pace differs from regular season so it needs playoff weighting.

nhl.special_teams.reason: Power-play opportunities are fewer in the playoffs but conversion matters; moderate contribution to goal mean.

nhl.penalty_rates.reason: Penalty counts feed power-play goal chances, but referee crews in the playoffs call fewer, lessening the effect.

nhl.injuries_pit.reason: Matters when a star or starting goalie is out; frequency per series is lowish, so secondary rather than primary for totals.

nhl.empty_net.reason: Empty-net goals are a small additive component of totals that rises with elimination and one-goal games; context for the tail.

nhl.league_scoring_environment.reason: Calibrates the level of goals per game by season; shifts the mean but does not differentiate series.

interactions.mechanism: A larger rating gap shortens the series (fewer games to add) while it also raises the favourite's scoring and lowers the underdog's, so total goals depend on length and per-game mean jointly: the product E[N]*mu is not the sum of separate effects, since length and goals are correlated through the gap.
interactions.how_to_test: Compare series-total model with independent length and goals vs a joint simulation, on 2005-present series, by held-out log-loss in bins of rating gap.

interactions.mechanism: An elite goalie lowers goals against, but when goalie volatility is high a hot or cold streak shifts both the number of games and the goals per game in the same direction, so mean quality and volatility multiply in effect on the total's spread.
interactions.how_to_test: Add goalie_quality x volatility to a series-total regression and compare residual variance by volatility tercile.

interactions.mechanism: Empty-net goals are rare in neutral states but common when a team trails by one late in an elimination game; the empty-net contribution to goals is concentrated in the elimination states, so its effect depends on series state.
interactions.how_to_test: Tabulate empty-net goals per game by series state and elimination flag and test the interaction in a Poisson regression.

interactions.mechanism: Overtime probability peaks when teams are closely matched and the regulation tie probability is highest; below a rating-gap threshold OT frequency is flat, above it falls, so the rating gap acts on OT goals nonlinearly.
interactions.how_to_test: Estimate OT share of playoff games by rating-gap decile and compare piecewise fit to linear.

interactions.mechanism: Early games reflect the regular-season matchup, while later games reflect adjustment and heavier playoff structure (fewer penalties, tighter checking); scoring drifts between regimes by game index.
interactions.how_to_test: Fit goals per game by game index with round fixed effects and test a break between games 1-3 and 4-7.

nonlinearities.shape: Expected series length rises concavely as per-game win probability moves toward 50 percent, reaching about 5.8 games at parity
nonlinearities.why: The mean of a best-of-seven saturates near parity and falls quickly as one team becomes a heavy favourite, so goals scale concavely with team balance.

nonlinearities.shape: Effect on goals against is roughly linear for ordinary goalies but compresses at the top because shot quality limits how much any goalie can save
nonlinearities.why: Goals saved above expected measured on regular-season shots tends to regress strongly in playoffs; extreme values are shrunk heavily, which makes the effect saturating.

nonlinearities.shape: Number of overtime periods has a geometric (heavy right) tail, with each extra period adding a constant hazard-based chance
nonlinearities.why: Sudden-death overtime has near-constant per-period scoring hazard, so P(k periods) decays geometrically, and the contribution of long games to the sum is small but not negligible.
